title: Variant tokenizer & tooling parity sweep and maintenance plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Context: As smart routing selects fallback model variants across regions and tiers, we must guarantee that tokenizer behavior, context-window semantics, and runtime tooling (streaming, function calling, KV cache offsets) remain compatible to avoid silent regressions. This ticket defines an operational sweep and ongoing maintenance plan for the Variant Compatibility Matrix focused on tokenizer/context/tooling parity. Goals: 1) Detect and fix tokenization drift between primary models and fallbacks; 2) Ensure context-window and KV cache semantics are consistent or mapped; 3) Verify runtime features (function-calling, streaming, structured output, special tokens) behave equivalently across variants; 4) Automate checks in CI and surface failures to Console/alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Golden tokenizer test suite added to CI that runs on all candidate fallback variants and primary models and fails on any tokenization divergence impacting >0.1% of golden prompts
Context-window mapping documented for each fallback variant, including required prefix/truncation rules and KV cache migration strategy
Tooling parity matrix updated with explicit pass/fail for: streaming partial tokens, function-calling schema compatibility, eos/special-token handling, and structured output transforms
Automated guardrail that blocks canary rollouts if parity tests fail for that region/tier
Operational dashboard tile in Console showing daily parity pass rate and top failing prompts
tasks: Inventory current fallback variant list and map to canonical tokenizer implementation (BPE / SP / byte-level)
Assemble 1k golden prompts set per workload category (chat, code, summarization, embeddings pre-tokenizer) and store in testdata repo
Implement tokenizer-parity-checker (Go) that compares tokenization and detokenization roundtrips and flags subtler differences (normalization, control tokens)
Add context-window simulation harness that validates identical KV-cache offsets and simulated prefix caching behavior between variants
Add runtime feature checks for streaming/function-calling by running end-to-end smoke tests against a variant matrix
Create CI job matrix (linux/cuda/quantized variants) that gates canary deploys when parity regressions detected
Instrument telemetry events to capture tokenization-mismatch counts, first-failing-token index, and request metadata (region, tier, route)
Create Console dashboard and Alert rule: parity-failures > 10/hour triggers PagerDuty to inference-sre
Write migration playbook for cases where variant behavior is intentionally divergent (documented mapping + compatibility shim)
Schedule weekly maintenance rotation for variant parity owner and add to runbook
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Strict parity for every tokenization edge (whitespace normalization, unicode normalization) would be costly. We will tolerate differences that do not change decoded tokens for the majority of golden prompts; threshold set at 0.1% initially.
Where parity cannot be achieved without large performance regressions, prefer a compatibility shim in the routing layer to normalize inputs before sending to fallback variants.
Check frequency: run full sweep nightly, critical canary checks on every deploy. This balances CI cost with safety for rollouts.
Telemetry retention tradeoff: store aggregated mismatch histograms for 90 days; raw failing request payloads kept for 7 days to support debugging while limiting PII exposure.
test_plan: Unit tests for tokenizer-parity-checker covering BPE, SentencePiece, and byte-level tokenizers
Integration tests that run golden prompt set against primary+fallback variants in the CI matrix
Simulated KV-cache tests that verify prefix reuse and offset alignment for each variant (including quantized builds)
End-to-end runtime feature tests for function-calling and streaming ensuring schema stability and partial-token streaming behavior
Performance sanity: ensure parity checks do not add >2% latency to nightly canary pipelines; if they do, move to sampled runs and add a fast-mode checksum
rollout_plan: Step 1: Land tokenizer-parity-checker and golden prompt sets in testdata repo (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ci/PR-1820)
Step 2: Enable nightly sweep for non-prod variants and surface dashboard failures to the inference-sre slack channel
Step 3: Enable gating CI matrix for canary/production deploys after 72 hours of stable nightly runs
Step 4: For any failing variant, automatically route affected traffic to next-compatible variant and mark variant as quarantined in the routing catalog
Step 5: Postmortem for any parity regression that reached prod; require follow-up fix or documented deliberate divergence with owner sign-off
